metaDescription: Free WYSIWYG Markdown editor with Mermaid diagrams, PlantUML preview, KaTeX math, diff comparison, merge, and table editor. No sign-up required.
socialDescription: Free WYSIWYG Markdown editor with Mermaid, PlantUML, KaTeX, diff, merge, table editor. No sign-up required.

guide.heading: A Markdown editor that runs in your browser
guide.lead: Nothing to install, nothing to sign up for — opening this page is the whole setup. What you write stays plain Markdown, and you can take it with you whenever you like.

wysiwyg.title: Write with the formatting visible
wysiwyg.body: Headings, bold text and lists appear the way they will read, without your having to memorise the syntax. What you write comes back out as plain Markdown.

diagram.title: Draw diagrams from code blocks
diagram.body: Mermaid turns a code block into a flowchart or a sequence diagram; PlantUML turns one into a class or deployment diagram.

math.title: Typeset mathematics
math.body: Write KaTeX notation and it becomes typeset mathematics where you wrote it.

table.title: Edit tables as tables
table.body: Add rows and columns by working in the cells, instead of counting pipe characters.

gfm.title: Use the syntax GitHub uses
gfm.body: Task lists and strikethrough are supported, so your document survives the trip to GitHub intact.

code.title: Colour your code
code.body: Code blocks are recognised by language and highlighted accordingly.

diff.title: See what changed
diff.body: Put two versions side by side, with only the changed lines coloured — then merge one into the other.

sync.title: Move between GitHub and Google Drive
sync.body: Open a file straight from a repository or a drive, and put it back where it came from when you are done.

guide.topicsLead: Diagrams, math, tables and comparisons each have a guide with the syntax and worked examples.

open.title: Open
open.body: There is nothing to configure. This page is the editor.

write.title: Write
write.body: A copy of your work is kept in the browser as you go. Close the tab and you can pick up where you left off.

save.title: Take it with you
save.body: Download it as a Markdown file, or save it to GitHub or Google Drive.

signup.question: Do I need an account?
signup.answer: No. You only authorise a connection when you choose to save to GitHub or Google Drive.

storage.question: Where is my writing stored?
storage.answer: By default, only in your browser's local storage. Nothing is sent to a server until you choose where to save it.

syntax.question: Which syntax is supported?
syntax.answer: Standard Markdown, plus tables, task lists and strikethrough. You can also embed Mermaid, PlantUML and KaTeX in the body.

vscode.question: Can I use it in Visual Studio Code?
vscode.answer: Yes. There is an extension that opens the same editor inside Visual Studio Code.
